title: behaviors
text:
answerui.behaviors generates the delegated event script (Registry.build_js) for handlers registered in Registry and defines browser.js to wire up AnswerUI’s shared browser modules.
Application handlers are stored in Registry as records containing a selector, an event name, a capture flag, and a JavaScript handler body. The generated script installs one document listener per event and capture phase, then matches the nearest ancestor for each rule’s selector when an event fires. Elements inserted by htmx work without attaching extra listeners. Built-in interactive controllers with local state are mounted through a MutationObserver in browser.js and disposed when their elements are removed from the document.
from answerui.registry import reg, hypelt
from fastcore.test import *

title: behaviors
text:
The runtime
_runtime is the entire client script. build_js embeds rules as an array of objects. Each object has sel (selector), evs (DOM event names), cap (capture boolean), init (boolean), and fn (handler). The script groups these objects by event name and capture phase, then installs one document listener per group regardless of how many rules share it. When an event fires on an Element target, that listener calls closest(r.sel) for each rule in the group and runs r.fn(el, e) on any match.
An init rule runs when matching elements enter the document. When rules includes any init rule, the script registers a callback with htmx.onLoad. htmx calls that callback with document.body on initial load and with the root element of each swapped fragment. The callback checks root itself (root.matches) and its descendants (root.querySelectorAll). Checking ancestors instead would re-run init handlers on outer elements already in the page. Each init call passes a synthetic new Event('init') that is never dispatched. Load htmx before this script whenever you register init rules. FastHTML’s default headers and demo both include htmx first.
The script executes once per document. FastHTML sends page headers only with full pages, never with htmx fragment responses. When htmx swaps a full page, it discards the incoming <head>.
Each handler is an async function. If one throws, the returned promise is rejected without stopping other handlers registered for the same event. Capture-phase listening (cap=True) is opt-in for non-bubbling events such as toggle and scroll. A regenerated script takes effect cleanly only in a fresh page or preview. Injecting a second copy into the same document attaches duplicate listeners alongside the existing ones.

title: behaviors
text:
Entries
_entry formats each behavior record as one object literal in rules. AnswerUI defines two special event names. init runs when an element enters the document. cleanup runs before an element is removed by htmx. Every other name is a DOM event. A leading : expands to htmx: (for example, ':after-request' becomes 'htmx:after-request').
htmx dispatches events under three naming conventions. htmx 2 dispatches camelCase names such as htmx:afterSwap together with hyphenated aliases such as htmx:after-swap. htmx 4 uses colon-separated names such as htmx:after:swap. FastHTML’s htmx4=True sets metaCharacter to -, turning every colon into a hyphen (htmx-after-swap). _event normalizes these spellings to htmx: followed by the hyphenated name. _spellings expands a canonical htmx event back into all three DOM event names. The script registers listeners for all three because only one fires on a given page.
init and cleanup are handled separately. Because init is not a DOM event, _spellings('init') returns [] and the script invokes init handlers through htmx.onLoad across both htmx versions. For cleanup, _spellings returns _cleanup, which lists htmx 2’s hyphenated alias (htmx:before-cleanup-element), htmx 4’s htmx:before:cleanup, and FastHTML’s htmx-before-cleanup. Under htmx 4, cleanup fires only for elements initialised by htmx (elements with hx- attributes). Each distinct handler body becomes one async function taking (el, e), declared before rules and referenced by name in each entry:
_event normalizes every htmx event spelling to the same canonical name. _spellings returns the DOM event names registered for it:

for ev in [':after-swap', 'htmx:afterSwap', 'htmx:after:swap', 'htmx-after-swap']: test_eq(_event(ev), 'htmx:after-swap')
_spellings('htmx:after-swap')

['htmx:after-swap', 'htmx:after:swap', 'htmx-after-swap']

title: behaviors
text:
Building the script
A behavior is identified by (selector, canonical_event, capture), using _event to canonicalize the event name. Declaring the same identity again replaces the earlier handler. Only the last declaration in registry order appears in the script. Because re-registering a rule preserves its original position in self.rules, re-running a component definition cannot overwrite an application rule registered later. Replacing a handler also keeps the identity’s original position in the output dict to preserve execution order. Because Registry compares selector strings literally without parsing CSS, two distinct selectors matching the same element are separate behaviors. Both handlers run.
behaviors returns the effective handler for each identity along with its declaring rule key. build_js deduplicates identical handler bodies and assembles the script:



Registry.build_js
def build_js():
The behavior script: one function per distinct handler, one entry per effective behavior





Registry.behaviors
def behaviors():
The effective behavior per (selector, event, capture): the last declared in registry order, with the key of the rule that declared it


This example defines a NoticeBox component with two behaviors: an init handler that removes the element after an autodismiss delay, and a click handler on [dismiss]. Because htmx calls htmx.onLoad only for the initial page and newly swapped fragments, swapping content inside an existing notice-box does not restart its timer:

NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', layer='components', doc='A notice that dismisses itself.', on={
    ('&[autodismiss]', 'init'): r"await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, +el.getAttribute('autodismiss'))); el.remove()",
    ('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"el.closest('notice-box').remove()"})
print('\n'.join(l for l in reg.build_js().splitlines() if 'notice-box' in l))

async function f1(el, e) { el.closest('notice-box').remove() }
const rules = [{sel: ":is(notice-box)[autodismiss]", evs: [], cap: false, init: true, fn: f0},
{sel: ":is(notice-box) [dismiss]", evs: ["click"], cap: false, init: false, fn: f1}];


The init entry has init: true and evs: [] because htmx.onLoad invokes it instead of a document listener. The click entry has init: false. build_js emits the handler functions and rules array. At page load, the script groups those entries into document listeners.
You can register the same handler body for multiple events in one rule. Here a form is marked dirty on input and on change (a <select> fires only change). Registering the input handler again in an anonymous rule keeps the change handler in place because anonymous rule keys include their behaviors. build_js declares the shared handler function once and references it from both entries:

_dirty = r"el.toggleAttribute('dirty', [...el.elements].some(c => c.value !== c.defaultValue))"
reg.rule(name='dirty', sel='form', on={('&', 'input'): _dirty, ('&', 'change'): _dirty})
reg.rule(sel='form', on={('&', 'input'): _dirty})
s = reg.build_js()
test_eq(s.count(_dirty), 1)
test_eq(s.count('":is(form)"'), 2)

To require confirmation before dismissing a notice, register the same selector and event on NoticeBox. Just as in the component definition, & expands to :is(notice-box). Because the behavior identity matches, the confirmation handler replaces the original. Each effective behavior’s rule field holds the key of the rule that supplied its active handler:

NoticeBox.rule('confirm-dismiss', on={('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"if (confirm('Dismiss this notice?')) el.closest('notice-box').remove()"})
{k: b['rule'] for k,b in reg.behaviors().items()}

{(':is(notice-box)[autodismiss]', 'init', False): 'NoticeBox.base',
 (':is(notice-box) [dismiss]', 'click', False): 'NoticeBox.confirm-dismiss',
 (':is(form)', 'input', False): '858472c34654',
 (':is(form)', 'change', False): 'dirty'}


The generated script contains only the confirmation click handler for [dismiss]. NoticeBox.behaviors still lists both declarations made on the component. reg.behaviors returns only the effective handlers emitted to the script:

s = reg.build_js()
test_eq(s.count('":is(notice-box) [dismiss]"'), 1)
assert 'confirm(' in s
NoticeBox.behaviors

[{'sel': ':is(notice-box)[autodismiss]',
  'ev': 'init',
  'js': "await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, +el.getAttribute('autodismiss'))); el.remove()",
  'cap': False},
 {'sel': ':is(notice-box) [dismiss]',
  'ev': 'click',
  'js': "el.closest('notice-box').remove()",
  'cap': False},
 {'sel': ':is(notice-box) [dismiss]',
  'ev': 'click',
  'js': "if (confirm('Dismiss this notice?')) el.closest('notice-box').remove()",
  'cap': False}]


Re-registering the component’s definition does not displace the application’s override:

NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', layer='components', doc='A notice that dismisses itself.', on={
    ('&[autodismiss]', 'init'): r"await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, +el.getAttribute('autodismiss'))); el.remove()",
    ('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"el.closest('notice-box').remove()"})
test_eq(reg.behaviors()[(':is(notice-box) [dismiss]', 'click', False)]['rule'], 'NoticeBox.confirm-dismiss')
[k for k in reg.behaviors() if k[1]=='init']

[(':is(notice-box)[autodismiss]', 'init', False)]

title: behaviors
controls
text:
Btn
Buttons are raised at rest and sunken while pressed. Pressing shifts the label, bevels, and shadows without changing outer dimensions. A row of buttons stays aligned regardless of which ones are pressed.
Three ARIA attributes hold a button in its sunken state without shifting the label: aria-busy="true" for an in-flight request, aria-pressed="true" for a latched toggle, and aria-expanded="true" for an open popover or menu. Each variant controls that appearance through --ui-held-face and --ui-held-shadow.
A busy button fades its label and shows a centred spinner without resizing. Because aria-busy="true" changes appearance only, users can still click a busy button. Set disabled to prevent activation.
When a button triggers an htmx request, htmx adds the htmx-request class while the request runs. The busy appearance waits for --busy-delay (default 200ms) to avoid flashing on fast requests. Server-set aria-busy="true" appears immediately. When a form triggers the request, htmx adds htmx-request to the form instead of the button. Set hx-indicator on the form to target the button.
A disabled button is flat and faded with no shadow while retaining its variant colour. Re-enabling it restores the raised appearance.
The default primary variant uses the accent colour. variant='secondary' uses the neutral surface colour with a hairline border. variant='quiet' has no background, border, or shadow at rest and inherits the parent text colour. Hovering a quiet button applies --tint (8% alpha). Pressing or holding it applies a 12% tint.
Pass size='sm' or size='lg' to set btn-size for compact or prominent actions (None uses the default size).
Pass href to render an <a> styled as a button, with the same variants, sizes, and icon option (omitting type). Because links have no native disabled state, :disabled styling does not apply to them. Handwritten <a btn href="..."> elements match the same rules.



Btn
def Btn(
    *c, variant:str='primary', size:NoneType=None, href:NoneType=None, type:str='button', icon:bool=False, **attrs
):
A raised action, latched by aria-pressed and sunken while busy or expanded


Each variant, size, and state in a wrapping cluster: default, secondary, quiet, a link, small and large sizes, danger and success tones, disabled, busy, and latched:

Btn.demo()


  
↻  



Passing href emits an <a> without type, and size sets btn-size only when given:

link = Btn('Sign up', href='/signup', variant='secondary', size='lg')
test_eq(link.tag, 'a')
assert 'type' not in link.attrs
test_eq(link.attrs['btn-size'], 'lg')
assert Btn('Save').attrs.get('btn-size') is None
to_xml(link)

'<a href="/signup" btn btn-variant="secondary" btn-size="lg">Sign up</a>'


Custom variants can override resting padding (--ui-pad-block, --ui-pad-inline) or --relief without redefining the pressed state. Below, compact tightens padding and flat sets --relief: 0. Both variants are registered on Btn for this notebook rather than built in. doc(Btn) lists them while they remain registered. To reduce depth across an entire application, set :root { --relief: .5; }.

Btn.variant('compact', '--ui-pad-block: var(--space-3); --ui-pad-inline: var(--space-2);', doc='Tighter padding.')
Btn.variant('flat', '--relief: 0;', doc='No rims, shadows, or displacement.')

Btn.flat [app] :is([btn])[flat]: No rims, shadows, or displacement.


Flat buttons show their colour states without bevels, shadows, or label shift. The two Pin buttons compare unselected (aria-pressed="false") and selected (aria-pressed="true"):

demo(Cluster(
    Btn('Compact', compact=True), Btn('Flat', flat=True),
    Btn('Pin', variant='secondary', flat=True, aria_pressed='false'),
    Btn('Pin', variant='secondary', flat=True, aria_pressed='true'),
    cls='gap-2'))


  
↻  



Pass icon=True for an icon-only button to make its horizontal padding match its vertical padding (--ui-pad-inline: var(--ui-pad-block)). Always supply an aria-label because an icon has no accessible name. Buttons containing both an icon and text use standard button padding.
Three square icon-only close buttons (primary, secondary, quiet) beside a labelled icon button and a text-only button:

close = [Btn(X(), icon=True, aria_label='Close'), Btn(X(), icon=True, aria_label='Close', variant='secondary'),
    Btn(X(), icon=True, aria_label='Close', variant='quiet')]
demo(Cluster(*close, Btn(X(), 'Close', variant='secondary'), Btn('Save'), cls='gap-2'))

text:
Text controls
Text controls use inverted bevel lighting (--bevel-in and --sunken) to look recessed into the page like a well. Disabled controls flatten to a muted background without the sunken shadow. Input, Textarea, and Select add the input, textarea, and select marker attributes. Handwritten HTML with the same attributes matches the same CSS rules. Input rejects type='checkbox', type='radio', and type='range' so well styling is not applied by mistake; use Checkbox, Radio, or Range instead, and use FastHTML’s unmarked Input for file pickers or button-type inputs.
Number inputs (type="number") hide browser spin buttons while keeping keyboard arrow stepping.

title: controls
text:
Enabling a button
Render a submit button disabled with an enable attribute to enable it automatically when form conditions are met. Set enable="changed" to wait until any control differs from its initial rendered value. Set enable="valid" to wait until the form passes native validation, or enable="changed valid" to require both.
The shared form handler compares each control against its browser default (defaultValue, defaultChecked, or defaultSelected) without storing a separate snapshot. Resetting the form disables the button again. Forms swapped in by htmx work the same way because the browser treats their rendered values as defaults.
Change the name or enter a valid required email address to enable Save. Clicking Reset restores the initial values and disables Save again:

demo(Form(Input(name='name', value='Ada', aria_label='Display name'), Input(name='email', type='email', required=True, placeholder='Email', aria_label='Email'),
    Cluster(Btn('Save', type='submit', disabled=True, enable='changed valid'), Btn('Reset', type='reset', variant='secondary')), stack=True, style='inline-size: 24rem'))

Copy
Copy renders a quiet button (icon-only by default, with aria-label="Copy") that copies text to the clipboard. Pass copyfor with the id of a target element to copy a form control’s value or any other element’s textContent. Pass copy to copy a fixed string instead.
For 1.5s after clicking, the click handler sets the copied attribute on the button and swaps its icon to a check mark. If the button has an aria-label, the handler temporarily sets it to 'Copied' so screen readers announce the confirmation. Buttons with visible text labels are left unchanged. The Clipboard API requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost).

title: controls
text:
Click to edit
Use Btn(..., variant='editable') for values that are read far more often than edited. It renders a full-width button with the same padding and corner radius as a text well, bordered by a dashed hairline (--n) instead of a sunken surface. No input exists until the user clicks. Visibility does not depend on hover. On click, the application fetches and swaps in either a single input or a multi-field form. Inside a form, keep type="button" (the default on Btn). Set aria-label to describe the edit action because the button’s visible text is the current value.
The demo below uses a client-only rule to swap each value with its edit form. Click the name to open an inset input with Save, or click the schedule to edit day and time. Submitting updates the displayed value. Pressing Escape or clicking outside cancels and restores the previous value:

reg.rule(name='demo-editable', sel='[editable-demo]', on={
    ('& button[btn-variant=editable]', 'click'): r"const p = el.closest('[editable-demo]'); p.firstElementChild.hidden = true; p.lastElementChild.hidden = false; p.querySelector('input, select').focus()",
    ('& form', 'submit'): r"e.preventDefault(); const p = el.closest('[editable-demo]'); p.querySelector('button[btn-variant=editable]').textContent = el.dataset.text.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (_, n) => el.elements[n].value); el.hidden = true; p.firstElementChild.hidden = false",
    ('& form', 'keydown'): r"if (e.key === 'Escape') { el.reset(); el.hidden = true; el.previousElementSibling.hidden = false }",
    (':root', 'pointerdown'): r"for (const f of document.querySelectorAll('[editable-demo] > form:not([hidden])')) if (!f.contains(e.target)) { f.reset(); f.hidden = true; f.previousElementSibling.hidden = false }",
}, doc='Demo only: swaps the value for its form and back in place of the server; a click outside or Escape cancels.')

def _editable_demo(value, form, text, **attrs):
    "An editable value and the hidden form that edits it; `text` is the template that turns the form's fields into the new value"
    return Div(Btn(value, variant='editable', **attrs), Form(form, data_text=text, hidden=True), editable_demo=True)


days = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday']
demo(Stack(
    _editable_demo('Untitled-1', Group(Input(name='name', value='Untitled-1', aria_label='Name'), Btn('Save', type='submit', disabled=True, enable='changed valid'), inset=True),
        '{name}', aria_label='Rename Untitled-1'),
    _editable_demo('Every Monday at 09:00', Group(Select(*[Option(d, selected=d == 'Monday') for d in days], name='day', aria_label='Day'),

        'Every {day} at {time}', aria_label='Change the schedule'),

title: controls
text:
Field
Field pairs a control with its <label> plus optional hint and error messages so assistive technology announces them together. If the control lacks an id, Field generates one and links the <label> via for. Field sets field-inline on switches, checkboxes, and radios so the control appears before its label text. Because that inline label uses justify-self: start, clicking empty space to the right of the text does not toggle the control.
hint and error render as <small> elements below the control, with their ids appended to the control’s aria-describedby. Passing error styles the message with ui-tone="danger" and sets aria-invalid="true" on the control. Validation rules stay in the application. Field only displays the message you pass.



Field
def Field(
    label, control, hint:NoneType=None, error:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
A labelled control with optional help and error text


Native browser validation bubbles appear only on submit and never show when enable="valid" disables the submit button. Instead, the shared field handler renders the browser’s validationMessage inside <small validation ui-tone="danger"> under [field] when the user leaves a :user-invalid control or when submission fails. On a failed submit, every invalid field displays its message and the handler focuses the first invalid control.
While displayed, the validation element’s id is added to the control’s aria-describedby. Once the value becomes valid, the handler removes the <small validation> element and strips its id from aria-describedby. Server-rendered error messages passed to Field have no validation attribute and are left untouched by the client handler.
For form-level server errors, render <small validation ui-tone="danger"> (Small(msg, ui_tone='danger', validation=True)) inside the form outside any [field]. Editing any control in the form removes that form-level message immediately. A <small validation> element inside a [field] is cleared only when that field’s control becomes valid.
All control types in one form. The Username field shows both a hint and a server-supplied error. Enter an invalid address in Email and move focus away to trigger client validation:

Field.demo()

notes = Textarea(name='notes', aria_describedby='notes-policy')
field = Field('Notes', notes, hint='Keep it brief.', error='Please remove the account number.', compact=True)
assert isinstance(notes.id, str)
test_eq(field.children[0].get('for'), notes.id)
assert notes.attrs['aria-invalid'] == 'true'
assert notes.attrs['aria-describedby'].split() == ['notes-policy', *(o.id for o in field.children[2:])]
test_eq(field.attrs['compact'], True)
notes.attrs

title: Typography and density
text:
AnswerUI controls text size, spacing, and corner radius with three independent CSS custom properties: --text, --space, and --radius. Override any of them on :root for the whole page or on a [ui] container for one region. You can tighten --space in a dialog without shrinking --text. You can also enlarge --text in a reading pane without changing padding or corner radius.
from answerui.preview import preview

title: Typography and density
text:
Scales and tokens
Steps with negative suffixes are smaller than the base. Steps with positive suffixes are larger. The stylesheet uses spacing tokens for internal control padding and gaps between layout items.

Text (--text: 1rem): --text-1 (0.875), --text1 (1.25), --text2 (1.5), --text3 (2).
Space (--space: 1rem): --space-3 (0.25), --space-2 (0.5), --space-1 (0.75), --space1 (1.5), --space2 (2), --space3 (3).
Radius (--radius: 0.5rem): --radius-1 (0.5), --radius1 (2), plus the fixed pill radius --radius-full (9999px).

The token layer also defines font weights (--weight: 400, --weight1: 600), line heights (--leading: 1.5, --leading-1: 1.25), motion timings (--motion: 150ms, --ease: cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1)), and @keyframes ui-spin. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, --motion becomes 0ms.
Base tokens inherit to descendants. The stylesheet declares every derived step on all elements and pseudo-elements inside :root and [ui]. Overriding a base on a container recalculates every derived step inside that container. Set a base token to scale a whole region. Override a single derived step only for a one-off exception on one element, because derived steps are still computed from the base on every descendant.

title: Typography and density
text:
Base styles and scoping
Inside :root and [ui], the reset sets box-sizing: border-box and clears default margins on block elements (body, headings, p, lists, blockquote, pre, figure, figcaption, and hr). Form controls inherit font. Media elements (img, picture, video, canvas, and svg) use max-inline-size: 100% and block-size: auto, except height-only images (img[height]:not([width])), which keep their HTML height attribute with inline-size: auto and object-fit: contain. With block margins cleared, layout attributes such as [stack] and [grid] control spacing. The reset does not remove native browser focus outlines.
The base layer sets --color-background, --color-text, and --color-accent on :root and [ui]. It sets --weight, --text, --leading, and --font on body and [ui]. Headings use --font-heading (defaulting to inherit), --weight1, --leading-1, and text-wrap: balance. Heading sizes use --text3 for h1, --text2 for h2, --text1 for h3, and --text for h4 through h6. Links use --color-accent with text-underline-offset: .15em. Code elements (code, kbd, pre, samp) use --font-mono. small uses --text-1. Icons matching svg.ui-icon, svg[icon], or svg:has(> use) are sized to 1.25em square. Keyboard-focused elements (:focus-visible) show --ring with a 2px offset. Use .ui-divider for a 1px top border in --color-border. Unmarked tables and form controls remain unstyled native elements.
Add [ui] to any container to override base scales, colour scheme, or hue locally without loading a second stylesheet. Wrap an opaque widget and its popup host in [unstyle] to stop AnswerUI selectors from matching inside it. Ordinary CSS inheritance still passes through [unstyle]. Add [ui] to an element inside [unstyle] to start a new AnswerUI scope.

title: Typography and density
text:
Surface relief and shadows
Raised controls use --bevel and --raised. Sunken controls such as inputs use --bevel-in and --sunken. Both bevels model top-left lighting. With --bevel, --hi is on the top and left edges and --lo is on the bottom and right. With --bevel-in, those edges are reversed.
--hi and --lo are computed by shifting the oklch lightness of --face (default var(--color-surface)) by +0.16 and -0.16. Deriving rim colours from --face keeps highlights lighter and shadows darker in both light and dark schemes. Fixed palette steps cannot do that because their lightness order reverses between schemes. --tint is an 8% opacity tint derived from currentColor.
--relief (default 1) scales the alpha of --hi, --lo, and --shadow-color without changing labels or borders. Setting --relief: 0 hides bevels and control shadows while --face and borders stay visible. --floating uses --floating-shadow, which does not scale with --relief. Dialogs and menus still have drop shadows when --relief is 0.

title: Typography and density
Typography and density
Typography and density
text:
Optional fonts
By default, --font uses system-ui, sans-serif and --font-mono uses ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace. To use IBM Plex, load fonts.css and set --font: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif and --font-mono: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace. fonts.css declares IBM Plex Sans (400 normal, 400 italic, 600 normal), IBM Plex Serif (600 normal), and IBM Plex Mono (400 normal). Set --font-heading (for example, 'IBM Plex Serif', serif) on :root or a [ui] region to use Plex Serif for headings. Layout and spacing scales do not depend on fonts.css.

title: layout
text:
Component styles set internal padding. Layout attributes on the parent control spacing between child elements. Each FastHTML constructor returns a Div with the matching HTML attribute:
Put any of those attributes directly on a semantic element such as Section(..., stack=True) to match the same CSS rules without an extra wrapper.
from fasthtml.common import Article, Header, Section, Ul, Li, to_xml
from answerui.demo import demo

title: Layout
Layout
Layout
text:
Layout and visibility utilities
Prefer [stack], [cluster], [grid], [toolbar], or [flow] for standard layouts. Because @layer utilities comes last in the cascade, utility classes such as .gap-2 or .flex-nowrap also override layout defaults on [stack], [cluster], and [grid] elements without inline styles. For overrides and one-off arrangements such as class="flex items-center gap-2", @layer utilities defines spacing, flex, text, visibility, and responsive helpers:

Spacing: .p-* (padding), .px-* (padding-inline), and .py-* (padding-block) for steps 0, 1 through 4, and 6, plus .gap-* (gap) for steps 0, 1 through 4, 6, 8, and 12. Step 0 is 0; steps 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12 map to --space-3, --space-2, --space-1, --space, --space1, --space2, and --space3. .mx-auto centres a block horizontally (margin-inline: auto).
Flex: .flex, .flex-col, .flex-wrap, .flex-nowrap, .items-start, .items-center, .justify-center, .justify-between, .justify-end, .flex-1, .flex-none, and .min-w-0 (min-inline-size: 0).
Text: .text-center (text-align: center), .text-muted (color: var(--color-muted)), .truncate (single-line ellipsis with min-inline-size: 0), and .tabular-nums (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).
Visibility: .ui-visually-hidden hides an element visually while keeping it accessible to screen readers. .ui-hidden and [hidden]:not([hidden=until-found]) set display: none !important.

Add [responsive-layout] to a container to declare the ui-layout container (container: ui-layout / inline-size). Below 48rem, .ui-wide-only is hidden with display: none !important. At 48rem and above, .ui-compact-only is hidden instead. Neither class sets display when the element is visible.

title: layout
text:
Stack
Stack arranges its children in a flex column and stretches them across the available width. Setting gap on the parent puts space only between adjacent children, avoiding a trailing margin after the last child. The default gap is --space.
Every layout constructor accepts CSS lengths or token references (such as 'var(--space-2)') for its sizing options. Layout rules stay in the stylesheet. _layout prepends those custom properties to any style string the caller passes:



Stack
def Stack(
    *c, gap:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
A vertical group with space between its children


None of these children has a margin. The [stack] container sets the spacing between them:

Stack.demo()


  
↻  



For a tighter gap, pass gap. The constructor sets it as --gap on the same div, with no extra wrapper or styling class:

to_xml(Stack(P('Ada Lovelace'), Small('Workspace owner'), gap='var(--space-2)'))

'<div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">\n  <p>Ada Lovelace</p>\n<small>Workspace owner</small></div>\n'


You can also put stack=True on a semantic element. Here the section keeps its tag while matching the [stack] rule with the default --space gap:

demo(Section(H2('Profile'), P('Visible to the rest of your team.'), stack=True))

text:
Cluster
Cluster arranges short items such as tags or metadata in a wrapping flex row. Each child stays at its natural width and aligns centrally on the cross axis. The --gap custom property (default --space) sets both row and column spacing.



Cluster

A row of naturally sized children that wraps to fit



Cluster.demo()

demo(Div(_cluster_example(), style='max-inline-size: 14rem; border: 1px dashed var(--n-1)'))

Pass grow=True on one child in a Cluster to fill the remaining width and push later items to the far edge. Because [grow] also sets min-inline-size: 0, a long name beside action controls wraps instead of pushing the actions out of the row:

demo(Cluster(Code('FastHTML'), Stack(P('Ada Lovelace'), Small('Owner'), gap='0', grow=True), Code('Edit'), Code('Remove')))

title: layout
text:
Grid
Unlike Cluster, Grid places its children in equal-width columns. It fits as many columns as the container allows at a minimum width of 16rem (--grid-min) and distributes the remaining width evenly. When the container is narrower than --grid-min, a single column shrinks to fit instead of overflowing. Pass min_width to override --grid-min without adding media breakpoints.



Grid
def Grid(
    *c, gap:NoneType=None, min_width:NoneType=None, **attrs

Equal-width columns whose count adapts to the available width


Each column contains a stack with a smaller gap. Changing the grid’s gap doesn’t change the stacks inside it, because each layout sets its own --gap.

Grid.demo()

grow=True also works inside a Stack to fill the remaining height. In a grid of cards, passing grow=True on the card body aligns every card’s footer to the bottom regardless of title length:

title: layout
text:
Flow
Flow uses CSS grid with a default row gap of .5em (--flow-space) for short text sections containing headings and paragraphs. Any heading (h1 through h6) after the first child has an extra .5em top margin (margin-block-start), putting more space before a heading than after it.
gap sets --flow-space independently of the --gap used by Stack, Cluster, and Grid. You can nest a Flow with a smaller gap without changing the outer Flow’s spacing. For full articles that also style lists, blockquotes, code, and tables, use prose=True.

title: layout
text:
Composition
The page below uses a stack to space its header, project grid, and help text. The header has its own smaller gap and a cluster of metadata. The article uses flow for its heading and paragraphs. Each layout spaces only its own direct children, whatever layouts its neighbours use.

demo(Section(
    Header(H2('Workspace'), P('A shared place for the team\'s projects.'),
        Cluster(Small('3 projects'), Small('Updated today'), gap='var(--space-2)'),
        stack=True, cls='gap-2'),
    _grid_example(),
    Article(H3('Working together'), P('Pick a project to see its latest work.'),
        P('Use the inbox for requests that have not yet been assigned.'), flow=True),
    stack=True, cls='gap-8'))


  
↻  



The outer Flow sets a 2rem gap around the nested Flow. The inner Flow uses a .25rem gap between its two paragraphs:

demo(Flow(P('Before the nested flow.'), Flow(P('Inner one.'), P('Inner two.'), gap='.25rem'), P('After it.'), gap='2rem'))


  
↻  



To change a layout default across an application, override its custom property in the app CSS layer (for example, [cluster] { --gap: var(--space-2); }). For a single element, pass a spacing utility class such as cls='gap-2' (.gap-0, .gap-1 through .gap-4, .gap-6, .gap-8, .gap-12), pass a constructor parameter such as gap for custom lengths, or set the custom property in style. Use ordinary CSS or the flex utility classes for other adjustments such as centring a cluster with justify-content. None of the layout rules sets a background, border, padding, or outer margin.
